audience: People collaborating with an AI coding assistant in a desktop workspace
primaryJob: Recognize, preview, and open uploaded artifacts without implying their HTML content has been parsed into native chat UI
coreFlow: Scan host-known artifact identity and file metadata
Preview the rendered artifact when available
Open, save, download, or play the artifact

direction.name: Quietly premium workspace
principles: Let artifact content—not chrome—carry the hierarchy
Use a single cool-blue interaction cue against a restrained dark workspace
Keep artifact content visibly contained inside its rendered preview

preserve: Artifact appears inline after an assistant response
reinterpret: Turn the generic uploaded-file row into a recognizable artifact object
Group title, type, timestamp, metadata, and action into a coherent hierarchy
evidence: Artifact row uses a charcoal surface with a blue document icon
Current action is a right-aligned View button
The card spans most of the conversation width

preserve: Plan title and concise outcome statement
Phase count, file count, and scope cues
reinterpret: Summarize the full plan as a three-step inline preview
Promote plan-specific metadata without reproducing the full document
avoidCopying: Source-specific plan wording beyond the supplied example
evidence: Plan uses three phases and two affected files
Blue is reserved for active navigation and the focal step
Content is organized with thin borders, uppercase section labels, and code-like detail

assumptions: The primary surface is a desktop chat embedded in a coding workspace.
Artifact cards should support plan, image, and video content through a shared system.
The preferred visual prominence is quietly premium: integrated with the chat but clearly actionable.
The chat host does not parse plan sections, phases, risk, or affected files from the uploaded HTML.
